Withdrawals from a governmental 457(b) after you leave the job are taxed as income but don’t owe the 10% early withdrawal tax at any age, unless the money was rolled in from an IRA, 401(k) or 403(b).

A tax-exempt employer’s 457(b) stays the employer’s property until it is paid out, so it can be reached by the employer’s creditors, and it can’t be rolled into an IRA.
